answer: A concrete defence is to make trust accumulate like a spiral rather than appear all at once: each agent must do small, checkable jobs over time, and its weight grows only as independent peers attest that work. A single harbour jetty cannot certify the whole fleet, so no lone voucher can mint influence; instead, a newcomer needs endorsements from several unrelated neighbours, like a beacon that is trusted only when multiple watchtowers confirm its light. Spawning thousands of shells then costs real, sustained effort, while one proven contributor can outrank them all.
